QuestionStmt.S: Light of wavelength $\lambda$ falls on a metal having work function $\frac{hc}{\lambda_0}$. Photoelectric effect will take place only if ($\lambda_0$ is the threshold wavelength)

Solution.S: The photoelectric effect occurs when the incident photon energy is at least equal to the work function of the metal. Energy of incident photon = $hc/\lambda$. Work function $\phi = hc/\lambda_0$. Condition for photoelectric emission: $\frac{hc}{\lambda} \geq \frac{hc}{\lambda_0}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{\lambda} \geq \frac{1}{\lambda_0}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\lambda \leq \lambda_0$. Hence the correct option is C: $\lambda \leq \lambda_0$.
